Collaborating with partners, AIIB meets clients' needs by unlocking new capital and investing in infrastructure that is green, technology-enabled and promotes regional connectivity. The primary responsibility of the (Senior) Credit Risk Officer within the Risk Management Department is to implement AIIB's credit risk management framework to ensure sound management of credit risk. The candidate is expected to identify, assess, and manage the associated risks with underlying transactions with focus on equity, both direct equity and private equity funds, with a view to safeguarding the Bank's interests by minimizing potential losses. The candidate will be required to implement the Bank's investment risk framework and will report to the Head of Credit and Investment Risk. Responsibilities: Evaluate the equity investment risks of proposed transactions, identifying, measuring, and mitigating key financial, market, business, and execution risks. Make recommendations on deal structures and investment terms with a focus on balancing risk and return by ensuring adequate compensation for risks undertaken. Analyze macroeconomic conditions, country risks, industry dynamics, competitive positioning, and business fundamentals to assess their implications for investment performance and downside risk. Evaluate the sustainability of business models, earnings, cash flows, and growth prospects, and identify key risk drivers under different economic and market scenarios. Build, review, and challenge financial models, including integrated financial statements, discounted cash flow (DCF) valuations, comparable company analysis, and other appropriate valuation methodologies. Conduct sensitivity analysis, scenario modeling, and stress testing to assess the impact of changes in key assumptions on business performance, intrinsic value, and investment returns. Evaluate expected returns against downside risks, determine appropriate margins of safety, and recommend investment limits and pricing that reflect the underlying risk profile. Independently assess proposed equity investments, and review the assumptions, projections, valuations, and risk assessments presented in investment appraisal documents. Monitor portfolio companies, market developments, financial performance, and key risk indicators, identifying emerging vulnerabilities and recommending changes to investment exposures, risk assessments, or mitigation measures as appropriate. Contribute to the development and review of financial and investment risk management policies, methodologies, limits, and procedures, ensuring alignment with sound banking practices. Establish appropriate frameworks for assessing valuation risk, concentration risk, liquidity risk, and portfolio-level exposures, and communicate independent risk recommendations to investment committees and senior management. Conduct best practice due diligence and supervision in close collaboration with the investment operations departments, ensuring that AIIB's risk appetite statement is implemented and a proper risk-reward balance is achieved in all transactions. Closely follow the Bank's lending and investment activities at transaction origination, monitoring, and supervision levels, and advise on possible actions to mitigate the credit and investment risk resulting to the Bank. Requirements: Minimum 8-10 years of relevant professional experience in multilateral development bank(s) or global financial institution(s), ideally in private sector credit risk management, lending, project finance, and capital markets. Familiarity with AIIB member economies will be an advantage. Master's degree or higher in risk management, finance, or other related fields. Thorough product knowledge of structured financial products and equity investments. In-depth knowledge of credit and investment risk-related financial analysis, procedures, and systems in complex global financial services settings. Proven skills and working experience in equity risk assessment and supervision in major industrial sectors in developing economies. A solid understanding of direct equity and private equity funds risk management and quantitative analysis skills would be an advantage. Excellent oral and written communication skills in English. AIIB is committed to diversity, transparency, and inclusion. We believe our strength comes from having a team with the right diverse skills, experiences, and abilities selected through a merit-based competitive process. We actively encourage applications from people from both within and outside AIIB members, regardless of nationality, religion, gender, race, disability, or sexual orientation. The role serves as the primary liaison with OEM suppliers for all service-related matters, including technical support, warranty management, service capability development, and performance improvement. The position focuses on strengthening service operations, developing dealer and OEM dealer capabilities, enhancing technical expertise, and ensuring alignment with group standards, supplier requirements, and safety objectives. Key Objectives Drive profitable growth of the Product Support Service business. Enhance service capability, capacity, and operational performance across assigned territories. Serve as the primary interface between the business and OEM suppliers for all service-related matters. Support technical excellence, customer satisfaction, and service profitability. Develop second-level dealer (SLD) and OEM dealer service capabilities and operational performance. Ensure adoption of Group systems, policies, processes, and operational standards. Promote and strengthen a proactive safety culture throughout service operations. Deliver regular business performance reports highlighting achievements, challenges, risks, and growth opportunities. Key Responsibilities Supplier Relationship Management Act as the primary point of contact with OEM Product Support and Service representatives. Manage and coordinate all supplier-related service, warranty, performance, and technical matters. Collaborate with supplier Product Support teams to resolve operational and technical challenges. Facilitate cross-territory support initiatives to maximize service effectiveness and customer satisfaction. Partner with supplier Parts, Engines, and Technical Support teams to resolve complex product support issues. Develop and execute service marketing initiatives and customer support campaigns in collaboration with suppliers and the Center of Excellence (CoE). Service Performance & Excellence Manage supplier service performance KPIs and ensure compliance with OEM service standards. Lead initiatives related to Distributor Excellence Programs and Service Excellence requirements. Monitor and improve service growth, operational efficiency, and customer support performance across territories. Conduct regular territory service reviews to evaluate business performance, identify gaps, and create improvement plans. Promote and share best practices, success stories, and operational achievements across the network. Support business investment decisions that strengthen service capabilities while ensuring sustainable returns. Dealer Development & Network Support Evaluate potential and existing Second-Level Dealers (SLDs) and OEM Dealers. Conduct performance reviews and business assessments for dealer operations. Support dealer capability development through coaching, mentoring, audits, and operational reviews. Ensure dealers meet operational excellence requirements and OEM standards. Coordinate workforce development and service competency improvement programs within dealer networks. Technical Support & Product Expertise Provide advanced technical support to Service, Sales, Parts, and Customer teams. Support troubleshooting and resolution of complex equipment and technical issues. Assist in parts identification and technical product applications when required. Recommend parts stocking strategies to support service delivery, warranty work, and fleet maintenance requirements. Ensure availability and dissemination of OEM technical publications, bulletins, updates, and service information. Act as the technical escalation point for critical product support concerns. Warranty Operations Management Partner with Warranty Administration teams to optimize warranty processes and claim management. Review and provide technical guidance on complex warranty claims. Support local service teams in making effective warranty decisions. Liaise directly with supplier warranty departments regarding large or technically complex claims. Prepare technical failure analysis reports and warranty investigation documentation. Drive timely claim processing and follow-up on credit note issuance and financial settlements. Identify and resolve warranty process bottlenecks affecting claim recovery. Maximize warranty recovery and supplier cost participation across all territories. Develop corrective actions to reduce recurring failures and improve equipment reliability. Ensure every service and sales employee maintains an Individual Learning Plan (ILP). Promote maximum utilization of online learning platforms and OEM learning resources. Support the development of internal instructor capability and localized training delivery. Identify advanced certification and development requirements for technicians and engineers. Monitor implementation of OEM training and certification programs. Collaborate with OEM and CoE training teams to design business-focused technical training initiatives. Support succession planning and development of future technical leaders. Reporting & Business Analysis Develop and present monthly, quarterly, and annual business performance reports. Analyze operational performance, service profitability, warranty recovery, customer satisfaction, and technical KPIs. Identify business risks, opportunities, and service improvement initiatives. Prepare executive presentations for management and supplier reviews. Monitor trends and recommend strategies to improve productivity, efficiency, and profitability. Experience Minimum 5 years of experience in heavy equipment, diesel engines, power systems, construction equipment, mining equipment, or related service operations. Proven experience in Product Support, Technical Services, Warranty Management, or Service Operations. Experience working with OEM dealer standards, distributor excellence programs, and service performance frameworks. Previous experience interacting directly with global suppliers or OEMs is highly preferred. Experience developing dealer networks and technical capabilities is an advantage.
